description: The Two Pointers technique uses two indices moving through a data structure (usually a sorted array or string) to reduce nested-loop O(n^2) brute force scans into a single O(n) pass. Pointers can move toward each other, in the same direction at different speeds, or across two separate arrays.
important_details: Pre-condition: Works best when the array is sorted or when a monotonic property lets you decide deterministically which pointer to move.
Opposite Direction: One pointer starts at index 0, the other at n-1; move based on a comparison against a target/condition.
Same Direction: A 'slow' pointer marks the boundary of a valid region while a 'fast' pointer scans ahead (in-place array modification).
Two Arrays: Independent pointers on two different sorted arrays/strings, advancing whichever is 'behind'.
other_relevant_details: Always ask: can sorting the input first unlock a two-pointer approach even if the problem doesn't mention 'sorted'? Many array/string problems that look like they need O(n^2) or a hashmap can be solved with two pointers in O(n log n) with a sort + O(n) scan.

variations.description: Start pointers at both ends of a sorted array and move them toward the center based on how the current pair compares to a target condition (sum, area, capacity).
important_details: Requires the array to be sorted (or sortable without losing needed info like original indices).
At each step, exactly one pointer moves — determined by comparing the current pair's value to the target.
Guarantees O(n) after an O(n log n) sort, versus O(n^2) brute force.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(n) for the scan (O(n log n) if sorting is needed). Space: O(1).

problems.name: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

variations.description: A slow pointer tracks the boundary of the 'processed/valid' portion of the array while a fast pointer scans ahead, used for in-place array/string modification without extra space.
important_details: Slow pointer only advances when a valid element is found; fast pointer always advances.
Common for de-duplication, moving elements to one side, or partitioning in-place.
Final answer length is usually (slow index) after the scan completes.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(n). Space: O(1) — the key selling point over a hashset-based approach.

problems.name: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II

variations.description: Independent pointers traverse two separate sorted arrays or strings simultaneously, advancing whichever pointer is behind, to merge, intersect, or compare them in one linear pass.
important_details: Both inputs must be sorted (or become sorted during the algorithm, e.g. merge sort's merge step).
Loop invariant: elements before each pointer have already been fully processed.
After the main loop, remember to flush any remaining elements from the longer array.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(m + n). Space: O(1) when merging in-place from the back (as above) to avoid overwriting unread elements.

variations.description: A special three-pointer variant (low, mid, high) that partitions an array into three regions in a single pass, most famously for sorting an array of only 0s, 1s, and 2s.
important_details: Three pointers: 'low' boundary of the 0-region, 'mid' current scanner, 'high' boundary of the 2-region.
When swapping with 'high', do NOT advance 'mid' (the swapped-in value is unexamined); when swapping with 'low', advance both.
Generalizes to any 'partition around a pivot' problem, not just 0/1/2.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(n), single pass. Space: O(1).

problems.name: Partition Array According to Given Pivot
